blocks.html: A result sheet full of plain numbers is correct but hard to read. Formatting changes how data looks without changing the data itself. A well-formatted sheet helps the reader find important values at a glance.

blocks.html: Most formatting commands are on the Home tab, or in the Format Cells dialog box (Ctrl + 1), which has six tabs: Number, Alignment, Font, Border, Fill, Protection.

rows: Red for warnings, green for good results

items.html: Horizontal: Left, Centre, Right (Ctrl + L / Ctrl + E / Ctrl + R work in recent versions).
Vertical: Top, Middle, Bottom — useful when rows are tall.
Wrap Text: shows long text on several lines inside one cell instead of spilling into the next cell.
Merge & Centre: joins selected cells into one and centres the text — ideal for a title across a table. Only the top-left cell's content is kept.
Orientation: rotates text, e.g. vertical headings for narrow columns.
Indent: moves text slightly away from the cell edge.

blocks.html: A number format changes how a value is displayed while the stored value stays the same.

rows: ₹ 1,250.50 (symbol lined up at the left edge)

items.html: Increase / Decrease Decimal buttons show more or fewer decimal places.
Comma style adds thousands separators.
If a cell shows ##### , the number is too wide for the column — widen the column.

blocks.html: Did you know? Excel stores every date as a serial number: 1 January 1900 is day 1. That is why you can subtract two dates to find the number of days between them — for example, the days left until your board exams.

items.html: Borders: Home → Font group → Borders button. All Borders draws grid lines around each cell; Thick Box Border surrounds a table. Gridlines you see on screen do not print unless you add borders or turn on gridline printing.
Fill colour: shades the background of cells, e.g. light blue for a heading row.
Cell Styles: ready-made combinations such as Heading 1, Total, Good, Bad.
Format as Table (Ctrl + T): turns a range into a smart table with banded rows, filter buttons and automatic formatting of new rows.
Format Painter: copies formatting from one cell to others. Double-click it to apply to many places; press Esc to stop.
Clear Formats: Home → Editing → Clear → Clear Formats removes formatting but keeps data.

blocks.html: Conditional formatting formats a cell automatically only when it meets a condition. When the value changes, the formatting updates by itself.

rows: Marks Less Than 33 in red; duplicate roll numbers in yellow
Top 10 scores in green; below-average marks in orange
A bar inside each cell, longer for larger values
Green for high, yellow for middle, red for low values
Arrows or traffic lights beside values

blocks.html: Steps: select the marks → Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than → type 33 → choose Light Red Fill → OK. To remove: Conditional Formatting → Clear Rules.

items.html: Freeze Panes (View tab): keeps the heading row and/or first column visible while scrolling a long list. Freeze Top Row is the most common choice.
Find and Replace: Ctrl + F to find; Ctrl + H to replace (e.g. replace "Sec-A" with "Section A" everywhere).
Spelling: F7 checks the spelling of text cells.
Notes / Comments: right-click a cell → New Note to add an explanation; a red triangle marks the cell.
Protect Sheet (Review tab): prevents others from changing cells. Unlock the cells that may be edited first (Format Cells → Protection → untick Locked), then protect the sheet with a password.
Hide formulas: tick Hidden in the Protection tab before protecting the sheet.

blocks.html: The Page Layout tab controls how a sheet prints.

rows: Portrait for long lists; Landscape for wide tables
Repeats the heading row at the top of every printed page
e.g. Fit All Columns on One Page so a wide table does not split
School name, page number, date on every page
Shows and lets you drag the page breaks

blocks.html: Press Ctrl + P to see the print preview, choose the printer and copies, and print.
